headline: Women Gather at Seneca Falls to Demand Equal Rights and Suffrage
dispatch: Hundreds of women and men assembled at the Wesleyan Chapel in Seneca Falls, New York, on July 19 for the first convention ever held in the United States to address the civil and political rights of women. Organizers Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott presided over the opening proceedings. A Declaration of Sentiments modeled on the Declaration of Independence was set before the delegates for debate and signature.
answer: Seneca Falls Convention on women's rights opens, 1848
